question.leadin: The repulsion of Pickett's Charge at Cemetery Ridge secured victory in this battle for Union forces.
question.text: Identify this pivotal battle of the Civil War in Pennsylvania, where Joshua Chamberlain led Union forces in a downhill bayonet charge at Little Round Top.
question.clue: During this battle, Lewis Armistead valiantly led his brigade to the "high water mark of the Confederacy" when he broke through enemy lines near the "bloody angle".

swap.leadin: This general's "neckties" were formed using railroad rails he destroyed in one campaign.
swap.text: Name this general, who made use of scorched earth tactics in his "March to the Sea".
swap.clue: This general sent a telegram offering a captured city to Abraham Lincoln as a Christmas present.

question.leadin: Name these candidates in the Election of 1860.
question.text: This man was famous for introducing the idea of "popular sovereignty" and was largely responsible for the Compromise of 1850. He engaged in a series of debates with the eventual winner of this election.
question.clue: This "Little Giant" from Illinois who defended popular sovereignty in his Freeport Doctrine.

swap.text: Robert E. Lee defeated this Commander of the Army of the Potomac at Chancellorsville. This man was relieved of his duties just prior to the Battle of Gettysburg.
swap.clue: Darius Couch assumed command from this man after an artillery shell hit the cabin that served as his headquarters, knocking him unconscious.

question.text: This chief justice of the Supreme Court presided over the Dred Scott case. He assisted Andrew Jackson in the Bank War and also heard the Amistad case.
question.clue: After replacing William Duane, he ordered the end of federal deposits into the Second Bank of the United States as Secretary of the Treasury, but Jackson's bid to replace Gabriel Duvall with this man was a failure.

swap.leadin: Naval warfare has played a crucial part in military history, from rowboats to nuclear submarines.
swap.text: The Housatonic was sunk by the H. L. Hunley, a ship from this nation during the Civil War. This nation's ironclad Virginia also fought the Monitor.
swap.answerHtml: Confederate States of America (or the Confederacy, do not accept or prompt on “America” or equivalents)
swap.clue: Soldiers from this country attempted to invade Vermont through Canada during the St. Albans Raid.

question.text: One such target of suspension of habeas corpus was Clement Vallandingham, a member of this faction of anti-war Democrats. This faction helped to initiate the Pratt Street Riots in Baltimore.
question.clue: Those members were Harrison Dodd and Lambert Milligan.

swap.leadin: Name the following things about Civil War General George McClellan.
swap.text: Including conflicts at Oak Grove and Malvern Hill, this series of conflicts near Richmond between McClellan and Lee marked the end of the Union general's Peninsula Campaign.
swap.clue: This series of engagements that included the battles of Savage's Station and Frayser's Farm.

question.leadin: T-Bonus 2. Identify these cases from United States legal history.
question.text: Roger Taney heard this case as a circuit judge despite being Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at the time. It concerned a Maryland officer involved in the ejection of Union troops from Baltimore, and declared that Lincoln's denial of habeas corpus was unconstitutional.
question.clue: The defendant's trouble began with his burning of a bridge in Parkton, for which he lost his position in the Baltimore County Guards and was detained by General George Cadwalader in Fort McHenry, prompting Chief Justice Taney to argue for his release.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about massacres from American history, per part.
swap.text: Confederate soldiers massacred the African American defenders of this fortification located north of Memphis on April 12, 1864.
swap.clue: This fort that future KKK Grand Wizard Nathan Bedford Forrest ordered brutally destroyed because Black Soldiers were manning it.

question.text: This 1862 act, named for a Senator from Vermont, started the tradition of agricultural and mechanical colleges around the United States, often financed with the sale of public property.
question.answerHtml: Morrill Land-Grant Act of 1862 [or Land-Grant College Act of 1862]
question.clue: The movement to pass this act was led by Jonathan Baldwin Turner, and a second act of this name was passed in 1890.

swap.text: Other early works about domesticity were written by Catharine from this family. Anti-slavery preachers like Lyman and Henry Ward were members of this family, which nicknamed firearms called "[this family's] Bibles."
swap.answerHtml: Beecher family [accept Catharine Beecher; accept Lyman Beecher; accept Henry Ward Beecher; accept Beecher’s Bibles]
swap.clue: One member of this family wrote Dred, A Tale of the Great Dismal Swamp and was accused by Abraham Lincoln as the "little woman" who "started this great war".

question.leadin: Edward Ferrero's United States Colored Troops suffered heavily in the aftermath of this battle, since they were inadequately trained for an experimental assault.
question.text: Name this 1864 Civil War battle that Ulysses Grant called "the saddest affair I have witnessed in this war." It took place during the Petersburg campaign.
question.clue: Many of Ferrero's men, sent in to restore order, were executed or returned to slavery by the victors, who were led by a future Readjuster Party senator from Virginia, William Mahone.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about new technologies arising during the American Civil War.
swap.text: A response in part to General Winfield Scott's Anaconda Plan, this was the first successful submarine. It sank the USS Housatonic before it sank itself.
swap.clue: In an 1864 battle off the coast of Charleston, it became the first submarine to sink and engage another warship, but it went down soon after the USS Housatonic and was not recovered until 2000.

question.leadin: It asserted a territory's right to make slaveholding impractical by refusing to enforce slave codes in order to create a de facto free territory despite Supreme Court decisions legalizing slavery. FTPE.
question.text: Name this idea put forth by Stephen Douglas and named for the location of Douglas's second debate with Lincoln.
question.clue: What is this idea put forward by Stephen Douglas stating that slavery could be excluded in new territories if citizens didn't pass laws favorable to slavery?

swap.leadin: Answer the following about mostly bloodless wars.
swap.text: The only casualty of this British-US conflict was the namesake animal. This confrontation concerned claims to the San Juan Islands between Vancouver Island and the Washington Territory.
swap.answerHtml: Pig War [or Pig Episode or Pig and Potato War or the Northwestern Boundary Dispute]
swap.clue: After Winfield Scott negotiated with James Douglas, a standoff was reached that lasted some 12 years until arbitrage conducted by Kaiser Wilhelm I led to a boundary through the Haro Strait.

question.leadin: Identify the following about histories of the Civil War.
question.text: Taking its title from a George Frederick Root song whose first line states, "Yes we'll rally round the flag boys, we'll rally once again", this James McPherson chronicle of the war won the 1989 Pulitzer Prize for History.

swap.leadin: The hundred-plus enslaved people on this ship were purchased after Timothy Meaher made a wager with a New Yorker that he could successfully skirt the US ban on the slave trade.
swap.text: Identify this ship captained by William Foster that secretly made the Middle Passage by July 1860.

question.leadin: This ship's captain wrote the book Memoirs of Service Afloat During the War Between the States.
question.text: Name this Confederate raider, built in Britain and captained by Raphael Semmes, which was sunk by the U.S.S. Kearsarge off the coast of France in 1864.
question.clue: Its namesake "claims" awarded over fifteen million dollars, ruling that the country which built it was responsible for its actions.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Thomas Nast's cartoon "This Is a White Man's Government."
swap.text: The cartoon is an attack on this son of a banker, who ran against Ulysses Grant as the Democratic candidate for President in 1868.
swap.clue: This man earned the nickname "The Great Decliner" by his opponents after he declined the Democratic nomination but then wept during his acceptance speech. This New York governor was the first presidential candidate to metaphorically get the bloody shirt waved at him.
